startup.name: Mirabelle
startup.description: A personal robot chef that cooks fresh meals on demand at home. Consumer hardware, pricing and technical approach not stated. Team of 2 in Paris, Winter 2026 batch.

yc_acceptance.basis: The company is listed in the Winter 2026 batch, so acceptance is already known; this reports the prior. Starting from about 1 percent with a 0.6 to 2 percent band (yc_acceptance.md), raised to 2.5 percent because physical AI and robotics are priority areas and a consumer robot is memorable, held down because consumer hardware with a team of two and no demo is a high risk copyable concept.
yc_acceptance.why_it_fails: YC would most plausibly decline because home cooking robots have failed repeatedly on cost and reliability, the description gives no prototype, price or customer evidence, and a two person team in Paris has no stated robotics or food background. The idea is easy to say and extremely hard to build to a consumer price.

anchors.source: python3 -I scripts/base_rates.py --industry Consumer --years 2022-2026 --calibration-only: seed 32% / 43% / 57% cond 43% (n=21); Industrials 2022-2026: 42% / 48% / 54%, median 4 months to seed (n=11). Window cut: 10 months of a 19 month p75.
anchors.adjustment_reason: Cut to about 0.77 times the 43 percent ever anchor for the 10 month window (about 65 to 70 percent of eventual seeds close in that time) with a small lift for how hot physical AI and robotics seeds are in this period, held inside 1.25 times. A hardware company with two founders and an unproven demo gets no further lift. Forecast window: 10.4 months, from 2026-01-05 to 2026-11-17. Seed means a financing round above about $1M from outside investors that closes inside the window; the YC deal does not count. Per time_to_milestones.csv (Consumer median 5.5 months to seed, p75 19.0; Industrials median 6, p75 22.1) about 65 to 70 percent of eventual seeds close within 10 months. These odds do not rank this company against others.

bands.rationale: Small post YC round under $3M from angels and a pre-seed fund, the commonest result for a thin team. The 2022 and later seed 25th percentile of $2.8M in knowledge/tables/round_benchmarks.csv sits at its top edge. The standard $500K YC deal is excluded because the window counts only rounds above $1M.
Institutional seed near the 2022 and later median of $4.1M, in line with the 3.0M deal size in the current NVCA data cited in stage_benchmarks.md.
A larger institutional seed, which the 2022 and later 75th percentile of $6.5M and press reported 2026 raises (median $6.0M) make plausible but not typical.
Upside seed of a hot category lead investor; rare for a small team.

ladder.why_it_fails: A two person team building a physical cooking robot needs a working prototype that cooks reliably, and hardware seeds are judged on a demo plus a path to unit cost. Investors have seen Nomiku and Replenish fail on consumer appliance economics and Moley stall for years. Within about 10 months the most likely state is a prototype in the founders' kitchen, a waitlist and the YC deal, because a hardware lead investor will wait for a reliable demo and a bill of materials.

anchors.source: python3 -I scripts/base_rates.py --industry Consumer --years 2022-2026 --calibration-only: Series A cond 0% (n=9); Industrials Series A cond 0% (n=11).
anchors.adjustment_reason: Window limited: median months to Series A is 28 (calibration sample) so few companies reach A before month 19, and the conditional rate here counts only A rounds closing inside the same window. Reaching a Series A years later is common for companies with paying customers, so this is not the ever number.

bands.rationale: Thin Series A or extended seed labelled A, below the 2022 and later 25th percentile of $10M.
Central band around the 2022 and later median of $14.2M.
Strong growth round near the 75th percentile of $20M and above.
Breakout lead round for a category leader with fast growth, rare in any cohort of the data.

ladder.why_it_fails: A Series A in this window would require shipping units and showing repeat meal use, which is almost impossible for a hardware company 10 months into a two person effort. Consumer appliance rounds also need large capital for tooling, and the only analogs with an A, such as Replenish with a $3.8M seed, never showed it. Nothing in the pitch supports reaching A in the window.

anchors.source: python3 -I scripts/base_rates.py --calibration-only: Series B given Series A 44 percent known only (n=126), lower and upper bounds 8 and 53 percent unconditional. This is an ever number, not inside the window.
anchors.adjustment_reason: Set about 0.7 times the 44 percent conditional rate because newer batches show only 16 to 23 percent in B2B 2022 and later cohorts so far (right censored). It is an ever figure and is not in the window.

bands.rationale: Down or flat round below the 2022 and later 25th percentile of $25M.
Central band around the 2022 and later median of $37M.
Strong round near the 75th percentile of $57M.
Breakout growth round for a category leader, seen in only a few percent of Series B rounds in the data.

ladder.why_it_fails: Most companies that raise a Series A do not raise a Series B because growth slows against the A plan, burn rises faster than revenue, or the category consolidates around two leaders. Investors at B want repeatable sales or usage economics, and a company that grew on a founder-led motion often cannot show them. Analogs such as the acquired or stalled A stage companies in the cohort show that about half stop here.

anchors.source: python3 -I scripts/base_rates.py --calibration-only: Series C given Series B 36 percent known only (n=55); Series D or later given C 40 percent (n=20). Ever number.
anchors.adjustment_reason: Held at 0.75 times the 36 percent anchor because the cohort is small and late stage data is incomplete; counted ever, years outside the window.

bands.rationale: Thin or down round; Series C medians fell from $64M to $45M between 2018 to 2021 and 2022 and later (n=6 and 9).
Central band near the 2022 and later median of $45M.
Strong growth round for a company that has kept compounding, above the 2022 and later median.
Category leader round, rare and mostly seen for companies that won their market outright.

ladder.why_it_fails: At Series C the bar is a clear path to a very large outcome, so companies fail here when growth decelerates below what a late stage fund underwrites, when a platform owner or a better funded rival wins the category, or when the market stays smaller than the pitch. Only 6 percent of the calibration sample reached C at the known only count, and the survivors mostly had hard to copy distribution or technology.

outcomes.why_it_fails: Consumer kitchen hardware has a poor record in YC data: Nomiku raised on Kickstarter and was undercut by Anova and Joule before suspending operations in 2019, Replenish raised a $3.8M seed and its acquisition is unclear, and Byte closed after a $2M seed. A robot chef also needs tooling, safety certification and service, so even a working product tends to end as a niche brand or an acquihire.

analogs.outcome_summary: Raised over $1.3M on Kickstarter, was undercut by cheaper rivals, tried a meal subscription and suspended operations in December 2019.

analogs.relevance: Pod based home blender hardware, Summer 2014.
analogs.outcome_summary: Raised a $3.8M seed in 2016; YC lists it acquired but no acquirer was found, so the outcome is unclear.
Reportedly raised a $2M seed in 2021, cut staff in 2023, now inactive; cause not public.
Founders from Apple robotics building a laundry folding home robot; hardware seed timelines and shipping targets have slipped, funding scale unknown.

killers.risk: Cost and reliability: cooking is a long tail of ingredients, cleaning and safety, so a robot cannot do it at a consumer price.
killers.evidence: Posha sells a countertop cooking robot at about $1,500 to $1,750 after years of work, and earlier attempt Moley priced above $300,000 and stalled.
killers.mitigation: Restrict to a narrow menu with pre portioned ingredients and show cost per meal before raising.

killers.risk: Capital intensity: hardware needs tooling, certification and inventory the seed market will not fund for two founders.
killers.evidence: Replenish needed a $3.8M seed for a blender, and Nomiku funded itself with two Kickstarter campaigns.
killers.mitigation: Presell with refundable deposits and partner with a contract manufacturer.

killers.risk: Funded competitors move first with the same promise at lower cost.
killers.evidence: Posha shipped first units in January 2025 with TechCrunch coverage, and other countertop entrants are crowdfunding.
killers.mitigation: Differentiate on cuisine quality in the French market and a subscription of ingredients.

competition_now.name: Posha
competition_now.traction: First deliveries in early 2025; first batch sold out per press.

competition_now.name: Moley
competition_now.what: High end robotic kitchen costing above $300,000.
competition_now.traction: Years of delays and little consumer presence.

competition_now.name: Status quo: meal kits, delivery and cooking at home
competition_now.what: Cheap, flexible alternatives with no hardware outlay.

technical_complexity.rationale: A robot chef needs manipulation of varied ingredients, heat and knife safety, cleaning, food safety compliance and a consumer price target. A two person team can build a demo in months but not a reliable product, and the long tail of failure cases is a hardware and data problem.

who: Samsung or Bosch style appliance makers
takeover_risk.rationale: Appliance giants could ship countertop cookers but have not moved on full cooking robots, and humanoid makers target factories first. The risk is more that funded specialists such as Posha reach the market earlier than that a platform absorbs the idea.

evidence.claim: Consumers pay about $1,500 for a countertop cooking robot, and the first Posha batch sold out per press.
Commentators say cooking robots keep failing on the kitchen's stubborn problems, showing need but weak delivery.

roadmap.goal: A video of the robot cooking a full meal start to finish.
actions: Build a prototype that cooks five dishes unattended.
Record cost of ingredients and machine bill of materials.
roadmap.proof: A repeatable demo of 5 dishes with under 10 percent failures.

roadmap.goal: Show demand and a credible unit cost to a hardware seed investor.
actions: Collect refundable deposits from a waitlist.
Sign a contract manufacturer quote for 500 units.
roadmap.proof: 500 deposits and a quoted unit cost under half the retail price.

roadmap.goal: Ship units and show repeat use.
actions: Track meals cooked per week per unit.
roadmap.proof: Over 3 meals per week per unit after 8 weeks.

pros.point: Large daily problem and a memorable product category already validated by Posha preorders.
pros.evidence: Posha shipped and sold out a first batch at about $1,500.

pros.point: Robotics and physical AI are favoured by seed investors in this period.
pros.evidence: Industrials 2022 and later cohort reached seed at 48 percent known only with median 4 months (n=11) per base_rates.py.

brand.rationale: A human name suits a home chef the way Alexa and Rosie style names suit household assistants, and the French food link supports a premium feel. Name cohort rates show no outlier, so brand moves nothing in the ladder.

narrative.headline: A compelling consumer hardware idea from a two person team with no stated demo: seed odds are held below the ever anchor by the short window.
narrative.general_summary: Mirabelle wants to put a robot chef in the home. People clearly pay for cooking help, and Posha showed a $1,500 countertop robot can sell, but the category is littered with companies that ran out of money before reaching consumer cost and reliability. In the 10 month window the odds of a $1M plus seed are about a third: the Consumer and Industrials cohorts reach seed at 43 to 48 percent ever, and only part of that happens in 10 months. A Series A in the window is very unlikely for a hardware company. Hardware, capital intensity and a two person team are the main limits.

assumptions: Description is two sentences; no price, prototype or traction known.
Window is 10.4 months; Series B and C are ever figures outside it.
A web result dated after the as of date (Nosh One, March 2026) was ignored.
